html:
The Dutch West India Company (WIC) was a chartered company of the Dutch Republic, founded in 1621 with a monopoly on Dutch trade and war in the Atlantic: West Africa and the Americas. It was both a business and a weapon in the war against Spain and Portugal.

Its main ventures:

  • Raids. In 1628 Piet Heyn captured the Spanish silver fleet off Cuba, the company's richest prize.
  • Dutch Brazil. It seized Recife and Olinda from Portugal in 1630 and held the sugar coast until 1654.
  • Africa. It took Elmina in 1637 and Luanda in 1641, and allied for a time with Queen Nzinga against Portugal. It became a major carrier in the Atlantic slave trade.
  • North America. It ran New Netherland and its town New Amsterdam until England took them in 1664.
  • Guiana and the Caribbean. It held Essequibo and Curaçao, a hub of the slave trade.

War and debt bankrupted the first company in 1674. A smaller second company ran until 1791 and was wound up the next year. Its sister, the Dutch East India Company, was far richer.
